notes.title: 🎥 Third Person Camera Now Available & much more! - Hollowbody Patch #9
notes.notes:
Hey all, we have another update! The star of the show this time is the new fully featured third person mode. A much requested feature that I finally worked out a way to implement without breaking the traditional camera system.

The game will now offer the player two options regarding camera style when starting the game 'Classic' and 'Modern' these represent the original fixed camera mode and the new third person camera, this option can of course be switched at any time during gameplay from the Options menu.

Along with this new camera system I have put a lot of time into optimising aspects of the game that I felt were lacking alongside some improvements and balancing to combat and enemies. I have also made some significant changes to how the game handles loading of data, fixing issues with black screens during loading of save files and new areas.

Hopefully the game should feel a lot smoother now thanks to many small updates across the board. As always I'd love to hear your thoughts or any issues you may run into over in the Steam discussion forums.

Please note: Whilst I have tried my best to avoid breaking any previous save data when updating to Patch 9, due to the nature of the improvements in this update some issues may arise from loading old save files. I recommend starting a New Game save file where possible.

I hope you enjoy this new perspective on the world of Hollowbody! Here's the full patch notes:


Patch notes:


 Added Third Person Camera
 Added controller rumble support
 Added unique camera transitions for Third Person Mode
 Added camera zoom via aim button for Third Person Mode
 Improved camera transitions for First Person Mode
 Improved lock-on targeting in First Person Mode
 Improved enemy AI and player detection for all enemy types
 Increased Lurker movement speed and detection radius
 Improved navigation and attack logic for Hound enemy type
 Reduced core revolver ammo pickup from 6 bullets to 4
 Replaced second melee animation when using Makeshift Axe
 Reduced enemy collision size when colliding with player, mitigating instances of enemies blocking player in tight corridors
 Character Controller rotation moved to fixed update in tank controls and camera relative controls, mitigating stutter when turning
 Improved character movement and turning when using Classic (camera relative) controls
 Removed targeting reticule when playing in first or third person mode
 Removed delay and animation before restoring player control when using Repair Spray
 Fixed persistent issue with run toggle unreliability
 Adjusted trigger for nightmare sequence in Sewers
 Fixed issue with cursor appearing when using keyboard or controller in menus
 Locked mouse pointer to screen centre when game window is focussed
 Various visual fixes and modifications to accommodate Third and First Person modes
 Fixed issue with black image for autosave graphic in Sewers
 Removed red overlay for save game thumbnail screenshots
 Removed motion blur post-process effect and Quality Settings toggle due to Unity's implementation causing performance issues for some users
 Split Park/Residential Street into two scenes, significantly improving load times and increasing performance on lower-end devices
 Improved loading screen transitions, mitigating full black screens when loading a new scene or save file
 Increased Sasha run speed for beach prologue
 Increased Mica run speed slightly for exterior and interior locations


Thanks so much for your ongoing support of Hollowbody and Headware Games, It's been amazing to read all of your feedback and love for the game. With this update I'm hoping to finally take a bit of a break and think about whatever comes next for Headware Games 👀

Cheers :)

notes.title: The Restoration Update - New Content - Hollowbody Patch #6
notes.notes:
Hi all, I hope you've been enjoying the updates to Hollowbody since release.

Since the game's release I have been focussing on improving technical aspects of Hollowbody and fixing various bugs based on community feedback. Over the past weeks I took some time to reflect on more general feedback, in particular taking note of game pacing and narrative aspects that didn't quite hit the mark for everyone.

During this period of refection I looked back at my original design notes for Hollowbody and some of the aspects of the game that were cut due to time constraints and various other influences. There came a point in development where I had to really lock-in the game structure and focus on the core design work that would see Hollowbody through to release. Whilst I am very happy with how Hollowbody released and the fantastic reception it's received from players, there were some narrative threads missing from the game that contextualize Echo's place in the grand scheme of Hollowbody's story.

This update looks to remedy that. Alongside some additional interactions and puzzle sections added to the later stages of the game I've been working on a larger optional puzzle that spans several locations, with the solution hopefully clearing up some confusion players had about the city's restoration efforts and subsequent downfall. Keep an eye out for new inventory items or changes in the environment.

Patch notes:


 Additional puzzle section added to High Street Part 1
 Additional puzzle section added to High Street Part 2
 Additional puzzle section added to Underground Station
 Additional multi-stage puzzle added spanning several locations
 Four new small interior locations added
 Layout and camera tweaks in High Street Part 1
 Layout and camera tweaks in High Street Part 2
 Complete rework of cameras in Underground Station
 Performance optimizations for all exterior locations
 Run speed increased in all exterior locations
 Follow camera recentre time increased in all locations
 Tweaked pistol ammo drop rate
 Five additional achievements added
 Fixed issue with shotgun ammo not being saved/added
 Fixed text error where makeshift axe is called makeshift spear in inventory status
 Fixed issue where hammer can be picked up again upon returning to apartments
 Fixed issue with enemy visibility during certain cutscenes


Once again thanks for all of your support! With this update finished I'm looking forward to taking a bit of a break to recoup some energy for whatever comes next for Headware Games.

Cheers :)

notes.title: Patch 4 - Motion Blur, Return to Title and Melee Improvements
notes.notes:
Hey all, today's patch includes some bug fixes, requested features and covers some melee combat adjustments.

This patch will not conflict with your existing save files.

Patch notes:


Fixed minor texture issue in High Street
Fixed typo on discarded note
Fixed an issue where multiple melee weapons would show at the same time in Mica's hand
Added motion blur on/off option
Added the option to 'Return to Title' when selecting quit game

Melee combat improvements:

Changed Mica's default attack with melee weapons to swing weapon, regardless of lock-on state
Added the ability to turn whilst attacking with a melee weapon when not in a lock-on state
Sped up Mica's hit reaction animations that are used when taking damage
Reduced the time it takes to regain control of Mica when receiving damage by half 
Added unique button mapping for 'Stomp' - Now mapped to a single tap of Triangle/Y/Middle Mouse Button
Updated combat tutorial adding Stomp button prompt
Updated options menu text adding Stomp button prompt


Further information:

Motion blur can now be turned on or off in the Graphic Options menu.

The option to return to title screen has been added alongside quit to desktop in the Quit Game menu.

Mica will now recover from taking damage 50% faster, putting you back in control quicker.

Melee weapons can now be used without lock-on and Mica is able to change direction whilst attacking, this results in some more dynamic encounters when not using tank controls.

'Stomp' is now mapped to a single tap of Triangle/Y/Middle Mouse Button. In case you missed it, you can stomp the glowing ammo boxes on the ground.

Please note, you may need to restart your Steam client for this update to be available

Thanks! As mentioned before please let me know if any issues or improvements you would like to see in the Steam forums or Headware Discord. I'll keep patching as new reports come in.

Thanks for the continued support :)

notes.title: Patch 2 - Collision fixes, bug fixes and FPS cap
notes.notes:
Hey all, thanks for your support and enthusiasm for Hollowbody.

I've made another patch to address some issues that have been reported this weekend. This patch will not conflict with your existing save files.

Patch notes:


Temporarily lowered the requirement for the Logomaniac achievement by 1.
Fixed a gap between buildings next to the Sewers exit in the first Highstreet section.
Fixed a collision issue causing Mica to get stuck behind the camcorder table.
Added a flashing lights warning to initial start-up text.
Fixed z fighting issue in Apartment 1.5's bathroom.
Fixed a visual gap in Apartment 0.2's wall.
Fixed rendering issue on Roof during first person mode.
Replaced shotgun ammo in Watcher house bathroom with pistol ammo.
Fixed an issue when setting Lurker enemies on fire where the inventory would not close.
Fixed similar issue causing a visual bug when burning Lurker enemies in first person mode.
Fixed typo in Underground flashback.
Fixed out of bounds softlock in Residential Street near Watcher House.
Fixed collision issue on second floor of Victim house.
Fixed z fighting on platforms in Underground Station.
Fixed rendering issue when viewing Mica's Apartment cutscene on ultrawide resolutions.
Fixed issue with rain splashes appearing in mid-air.
Fixed issue with ammo boxes that were able to be stomped multiple times, resulting in infinite ammo.
Added return function to difficulty menu options on title menu.
Fixed an issue allowing Mica to use the Damaged Battery in incorrect locations during Apartments.
Fixed an issue allowing Mica to use the Train Ticket in incorrect locations during Underground Station.
Fixed a camera issue causing Mica to be headless when climbing the scaffold in first person mode.
FPS Cap - Renamed options to better reflect functionality in VSync dropdown in Graphics Settings.


Some clarification on the FPS Cap:

VSync in Graphics Options now has three options:

Uncapped - Allow the game to run without a FPS limit.
Target: Monitor Refresh Rate - The game will aim to lock FPS at your monitor's current refresh rate.
Target: Half Monitor Refresh Rate - The game will aim to lock FPS at half of your monitor's current refresh rate.

If for example you have a 120Hz monitor, setting VSync to 'Target: Half Monitor Refresh Rate' will cause the game to cap at 60FPS.

I recommend capping to either your monitor's refresh rate or half if you're experience heavy GPU load.

Hopefully that clears things up!

Please note, you may need to restart your Steam client for this update to be available

Thanks again everyone. I'll keep patching as things crop up.
